I found the cause, and it isn't in the game. The fix is a change to the test copy only. I haven't shipped a game build, so there is no ON HIS PC line, and the five checks still have to pass in the next full run on the spare PC before this is done.

**What was going on**
- These checks fail only on the machines with a real graphics card: the spare PC and his main PC's idle runs. The VM draws canvases on the processor and passes them every time.
- v34.90 shows it most plainly. It draws the same figure twice in a row, with no frame step and no clock between, and the two pictures differ by exactly 1 pixel in every case. When the graphics card does the drawing, it doesn't always give the same pixels twice.
- I ruled out the game:
  - Every clock-driven effect in the draw path is on the HUD layer, which these checks don't read. The only one in the world layer (the curved-build body sway) doesn't move between two identical draws.
  - The auto resolution step was already taken out of frozen redraws in v34.98.
  - None of the picture caches gives different pixels on a first or second draw.

**The fix (commit a673cf901)**
- The test copy's builder, `tools/mkfixture.ps1`, now adds a few lines to the top of the game script in the test copy.
- On any page opened with a query, every 2D canvas is drawn on the processor, the same as on the VM. That covers the full run's slices and the single-check runs (runchk).
- The robots and the camera open the page without a query, so they still use the graphics card and their 4K timing numbers don't change.
- The game file is untouched. Nothing changes for players, and the seed 4242 fingerprint is unaffected.

**Results on the VM after the change**
- v8.85, v8.89, v9.07 and v33.51 pass.
- v34.90 now fails on a different line: "the survivor tracer is drawn 19.1 over the round, his flash 21.6 up." This part of the check measures the line drawing itself, not pixels, so my change can't cause it. It's a separate real failure the full run had been cutting off from its report. I logged it in `alarms.md` so it gets its own job.
- I didn't add a check that fails on the old build and passes on the new one, as the task asked. The failure only happens on a graphics card, and the gate runs on the VM.

**What's left**
- The commit goes to GitHub with the next ship, and the spare PC's next full run will show whether the five pass.
- I'm not allowed to edit `stable-known-red.txt`. I asked the coordinator in `alarms.md` to delete the five lines once that run is green. My notes are in `tools/handoff/console/notes/01-241-redraw-not-steady.md`.
